text:
elaine: FYI canary with pooled-sockets enabled is showing ~0.45% of streaming sessions terminating with an empty final chunk + socket close. Seen in eu-prod and canary-2.

mohit: repro? any correlation with tenant or route?

elaine: small repro attached in logs (pasted below). seems to happen when socket gets reused across two different active sessions quickly. stack looks like:
```
2026-03-11T14:22:01.123Z INFO reuse_socket id=socket-78 reuse_count=7 tenant=acme-session_id=abc123 route=/v1/stream
2026-03-11T14:22:01.127Z WARN session-mismatch expected=abc123 got= (empty) closing
2026-03-11T14:22:01.128Z INFO close reason=protocol_error code=1006
```

elaine: note the header parsing on the second handshake returns empty session id. client sees just `\n\n` chunk and then connection close.

jun: could be header table reset when using HTTP/2 multiplexed pool? did the change to pooled sockets also touch our header sanitizer?

mohit: we didn't change sanitizer; we added per-socket metadata in runtime to avoid re-parsing X-Stream-Id on every request (perf win). suspicious that metadata stale when socket reused very quickly.

console-ux: this shows up in console as a generic `stream_close` event with reason `1006` and not as `pooled_reuse_mismatch`. that's making debugging awful. can we add a telemetry tag?

elaine: agreed — we have no metric separating `pooled_reuse_*` from normal disconnects. current rollout hides the signal.

sre-bot: alert: stream-drop-rate (canary-2) = 0.45% > 0.3% threshold. Incident created: #STREAM-POOLED-REUSE-17698

taylor: quick thought — two mitigations: 1) conservative: mark pooled sockets as tenant-scoped (no cross-tenant reuse) until we fix metadata refresh; 2) fast patch: on checkout, always refresh headers from bytes until we validate session id matches socket metadata. 1 is config toggle, 2 is code path.

mohit: 1) increases socket churn/cost. 2) costs CPU but local fix. which is lower risk?

jun: we can instrument number of pool reuses per tenant and set a soft limit before forcing a refresh. so try 2) + telemetry + short-term soft limit (reuse <= 3) in canary.

elaine: sounds good. also add a special metric label `connection_pool_reuse=true` and a sample log that includes both the parsed header and the metadata we had — makes the console show if mismatch happened.

console-ux: I'll add a small console tile for `pooled_socket_reuse` and show sampled raw events (masked PII) with a link to logs. rollout UX: we should expose the current reuse threshold per deployment so support can toggle.

mohit: I'll open PR to: a) refresh header parsing on checkout until session id validated; b) emit `pooled_socket_reuse` telemetry boolean; c) gate reuse count to 3 in canary. doing canary at 2% -> 10% -> 100% after 24h stable windows.

taylor: do we need a rollback plan? if refresh makes perf regress we can turn off pooling for the route via runtime flag. document the toggle in the console under 'Streaming Runtime Flags'.

elaine: one more: billing/quotas — there was a report that some clients got double-charge for the last token when a pooled reuse was interpreted as a new session. can we confirm?

mohit: likely when session metadata missing we treat as new session and create a billing record. I'll add a billing tag on the new telemetry to correlate `pooled_socket_reuse` + `billing_event` spikes.

jun: created an adhoc dashboard: https://playground.internal/redwood/dashboards/pooled-reuse (sample) showing reuse_count, pooled_socket_reuse rate, stream_drop, billing_dup_rate.

elaine: PR #4218 opened with the header-refresh patch, telemetry, and canary gate. putting it on today's deploy window.

console-ux: great — after the canary we should add a 'sampled event' link in the per-route details (so support can click and see header vs metadata).

elaine: TL;DR action items: Mohit PR + canary gate, Jun create dashboard (done), Console-UX add tile and toggle exposure, Taylor doc rollback path. I'll follow-up with the incident thread once the canary completes. :thumbsup:

mohit: will update this thread with canary metrics. thanks all.
